archetypes.name: migration-completeness
archetypes.rationale: The plan transfers sentinel ownership between two scripts; verify no callsites outside the listed files still depend on the old emitter side-effect and that split-ownership cannot arise at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan transfers `.step3-entry-plan-printed` sentinel ownership from `emit-design-plan-preview.sh` to `run-step3-review.sh --preview-only`, making the emitter a pure renderer. Check whether any scripts, skill files, or documentation outside the listed scope-files reference or depend on the old side-effect behavior of `emit-design-plan-preview.sh --variant step3` — specifically callers that relied on the sentinel being set by the emitter rather than the driver. Verify that the plan's removal of sentinel logic from the emitter is complete with no residual read/write paths remaining in the emitter, and that no runtime path exists where both scripts could conditionally touch the same sentinel file. Confirm that the plan's test-harness updates cover the migration cleanly — emitter harness drops sentinel assertions and driver harness adds them — without leaving any harness that still asserts the old ownership model. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-protocol-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: The plan defines a 12-key stdout-fallback allowlist plus ordering and precedence rules that must be stated consistently across three separate plan sections; contradictions there would cause silent state corruption at runtime.
archetypes.prompt_body: The plan defines a 12-key stdout-fallback allowlist and ordering rules — later terminal KVs overwrite earlier fallback values only when the safe result env was not loaded, while file-sourced values stay authoritative when a safe env was loaded. Check whether these rules are stated consistently across the three plan sections that describe the same protocol: the driver spec (`run-step3-review.sh`), the orchestrator consumption spec (`SKILL.md`), and the harness spec (`test-step3-orchestrator-fence.sh`). Verify that the 12 pinned key names are identical in every plan section that enumerates them, and that the 'later-wins' versus 'file-first' precedence rule is applied in the same direction in both the driver emit logic and the orchestrator parse logic. Check that the rc!=0 `LOOP_STATUS`/`TALLY_PLAN_REVIEW_STATUS` override rule and the 'normalize empty/invalid LOOP_STATUS to panel-failed' normalization are described at the same processing point in both the driver and orchestrator sections and are exercised by the harness spec. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
